Author: Deepak Verma
Bench: Deepak Verma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:65360
Court No. - 75
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 27564 of 2020
Applicant :- Upendra Kumar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Araf Khan,Balbir Yadav,Purushottam Dixit
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Chandra Prakash Yadav,G.A.,M.P.S. Chauhan
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The instant anticipatory bail application has been moved by the accused-applicant for enlarging him on bail in Case Crime No.81 of 2020, under Section 376 I.P.C. & Section 3/4 POCSO Act &
Section 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, P.S. Atrauli, District Aligarh.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Learned counsel for the applicant next submits that applicant claims parity with co-accused Somveer, who has been granted bail by coordinate Bench of this Court by order dated 12.03.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Upendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91013083/
1 4.

entities.text: Upendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that charge sheet has been submitted against the applicant and during investigation evidence collected against the applicant.
He next submitted that the applicant's case is different from co-accused Somveer, who has been granted bail by this Court.
The applicant is not entitled for any indulgence by this Court.
Hence, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant may be rejected.

5. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the submission advanced, the nature and gravity of the accusation, I find no good ground for anticipatory bail to the applicant in the aforesaid case.
6. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is rejected.
7. However, if the applicant appears and surrenders before the court below within two weeks and applies for bail, his bail application shall be considered and disposed of in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 15.4.2024 SKD  Upendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91013083/
